## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (three Suggestion findings and one inconclusive checklist item; nothing at or above the Important threshold) The PR is ready to merge: all 22 acceptance criteria and every other checklist claim that could be checked passed, and no reviewer raised anything at Important or above. Rule applied: rule 6 — findings below the threshold and an INCONCLUSIVE item remain → APPROVE with notes ## Code Review Findings ### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (3)
3 items 1. `tests/unit/test_memory_admin_widget_render.py` (`test_checklist_choices_and_labels`) compares the group-name choices with `sorted(...) == sorted(names)`, so it checks which names the checklist holds but not that they appear A–Z as criterion 8 asks. Dropping the sort in `groupNameChoices` in `src/sqllens/ui/memory_admin.html` would still pass. (raised by 2/5 agents; corroborated by file and described defect, since the two reports give different line ranges) 2. `src/sqllens/ui/memory_admin.html` `renderGroups` and `groupKind` treat a memory whose `groups` field is absent (`undefined`) the same as `[]`: it shows `untagged` with the hover text "No groups: every rule set can read it." and matches the `untagged` filter. The server always sends `groups`, so normal use does not reach this, but an absent field would read as a positive claim rather than an unknown state. (raised by 1/5 agents) 3. `tests/unit/test_memory_admin_widget_render.py` never combines the group filter with the type dropdown (criterion 10); the probe combines groups with the search box only, and every fixture memory has the same type. (raised by 1/5 agents)
### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (1)
1 item - VC-15: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The comment asserts a td's own max-width is ignored by this 100%-wide nowrap table and renders wider than 220px, so the cap is on an inner block. [src/sqllens/ui/memory_admin.html]
Evidence memory_admin.html:115-129 shows table{width:100%}, th,td{white-space:nowrap} (line 119), td.trunc{max-width:360px; overflow:hidden} (126), and .groups-cap as a display:block inner element with max-width:220px (129), matching the comment's described structure. Whether a td's own max-width is ignored and renders wider than 220px depends on browser table layout (CSS 2.1 leaves max-width on table cells undefined), and also on the existing td.trunc rule, which uses td max-width. This cannot be settled by reading source; it needs a browser render, which I did not run.
